cards.title: Prioritizing Your Next Store Improvements: SEO and Email First
cards.summary: The presenter ranks learning SEO (via a rank-tracking plugin) and email marketing as the highest-value follow-on skills for a WooCommerce store.
cards.use_when: You have a functioning store and are deciding which growth skill or project to invest in next.

cards.title: Install Node, Git and Shopify CLI before AI-assisted theme work
cards.summary: Set up the local toolchain (Node.js, Git, Shopify CLI) that lets Claude Code read and edit a live Shopify theme.
cards.use_when: You are preparing a machine to build or modify a Shopify theme with an AI coding agent rather than in the theme editor.

cards.title: Pull the live theme locally so the AI can edit real code
cards.summary: Use shopify theme pull to copy the store's current live theme into a clean project folder, giving the AI agent read/write access to actual theme files.
cards.use_when: You are about to have an AI agent customise a Shopify theme and need the live theme files on your machine first.

cards.title: Add products and collections before generating the store
cards.summary: Seed the store with real products first so the AI designs the homepage and PDPs around actual catalog data rather than placeholders.
cards.use_when: You are starting an AI-assisted store build and need something for the design to be built around.

cards.title: Organise a local asset folder as the AI's design brief
cards.summary: Compile screenshots of desired theme sections plus your own logos, product photos and lifestyle images into one folder the AI reads as visual constraints.
cards.use_when: You are briefing an AI agent to build a homepage or theme and need it to match a specific look instead of guessing.

cards.title: Prompt the AI to interview you before it builds
cards.summary: Kick off a theme build with a prompt that makes the agent explore the theme and assets, ask about brand direction, and propose a plan instead of generating everything at once.
cards.use_when: You are starting a store build or major redesign and want controlled, reviewable output rather than a single giant generation.

cards.title: Build the homepage section by section in plain English
cards.summary: Have the AI generate one homepage section at a time, review it in a private preview, request plain-English tweaks, then explicitly move to the next section.
cards.use_when: You are generating or redesigning a homepage and want to catch layout and content problems before they compound.

cards.title: Preview changes privately on a local dev server
cards.summary: Run a private local preview of the AI-built theme, using the store's Shopify-generated password, so you can review each section before anything goes public.
cards.use_when: You are iterating on theme code and need to see changes live without exposing them to customers.

cards.title: Use easing and scroll animations to soften load friction
cards.summary: Ask the agent to add entry and scroll animations so sections fade in rather than snapping onto the screen.
cards.use_when: A page feels harsh or unpolished because everything renders instantly on load.

cards.title: Push the AI-built theme, then keep editing it in Shopify
cards.summary: Upload the finished theme to Shopify unpublised, verify it in the theme editor and on mobile, and keep using Shopify's native editor for manual changes.
cards.use_when: Your AI-assisted theme build is done and you need to review, adjust and prepare it for publishing.

cards.title: Configure shipping zones, free-shipping thresholds and taxes
cards.summary: Set up Shopify Payments, a single free-shipping zone with an order minimum and transit time, delete unwanted zones, and confirm tax regions.
cards.use_when: You are finishing back-office configuration before taking orders.

cards.title: Generate policy pages from templates and AI, then publish
cards.summary: Fill in Refund, Privacy and Terms policies using Shopify templates, write a custom shipping policy with AI, and publish them so footer links appear.
cards.use_when: You need the legal pages that checkout and the theme footer link to before you remove the store password.

cards.title: Connect a custom domain and go live
cards.summary: Replace the default myshopify.com domain with a purchased .com, then publish the theme and remove the store password.
cards.use_when: You are finalising the store for public launch.

cards.title: WordPress + WooCommerce baseline stack with Astra and Elementor
cards.summary: Set up a new WooCommerce store on WordPress using the Astra theme and Elementor page builder instead of the default block editor.
cards.use_when: Standing up a brand-new store from scratch and choosing your theme and page builder before building any pages or products.

cards.title: Creating mobile-specific layouts with Elementor responsive toggles
cards.summary: Build separate mobile and desktop section layouts by duplicating containers and using Elementor's Hide on mobile/tablet/desktop toggles.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a homepage or landing page where the desktop layout (e.g. wide hero with side-by-side blocks) would break or read poorly on phones.

cards.title: Building WooCommerce variable products with color/size variations
cards.summary: Configure a variable product so each variation (e.g. per color) has its own SKU, stock level and price.
cards.use_when: Listing a product that comes in multiple colors, sizes or options where each variant needs separate inventory and pricing.

cards.title: Connecting Stripe and PayPal payments in WooCommerce
cards.summary: Install the Stripe and PayPal WooCommerce gateway plugins, connect the accounts, run the connection test, and switch from Test to Live mode.
cards.use_when: Enabling card and PayPal checkout on a new store before going live.

cards.title: Configuring shipping zones with flat rate vs free-shipping thresholds
cards.summary: Set up WooCommerce shipping zones and choose between a flat rate and a free-shipping minimum to shape buyer incentive.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to charge for shipping and whether to offer a free-shipping threshold to lift average order value.

cards.title: Setting up a first-purchase welcome coupon with usage controls
cards.summary: Create a one-per-customer discount coupon to drive first orders while limiting abuse.
cards.use_when: Launching a store or running an acquisition push where you want a first-purchase incentive without unlimited reuse.

cards.title: Set up WooCommerce variable products with generated variations
cards.summary: Configure a variable product end-to-end: attributes, generated variations, per-variation SKU, price, stock and thumbnail.
cards.use_when: Adding a product that comes in multiple colors, sizes or other options on a WooCommerce store.

cards.title: Product data fields that drive PDP content: SKU, stock, weight
cards.summary: Fill WooCommerce Product Data tabs so stock messaging, shipping and descriptions match what the shopper sees.
cards.use_when: Creating or auditing a physical product listing on WooCommerce before it goes live.

cards.title: Configure Stripe and PayPal for WooCommerce and switch to live
cards.summary: Install payment plugins, connect accounts, run the connection test and flip the mode from Test to Live before launch.
cards.use_when: Enabling credit card and PayPal checkout on a WooCommerce store.

cards.title: Shipping zones, flat rate and free-shipping thresholds
cards.summary: Build shipping zones with a flat rate plus a free-shipping method gated by an order minimum, ordered so free shipping wins.
cards.use_when: Setting up shipping charges and a free-shipping minimum for an online store.

cards.title: Welcome coupon setup: percentage, usage limits, exclusions
cards.summary: Create a first-order welcome coupon with a percentage discount and a one-use-per-customer limit.
cards.use_when: Launching a store or promo and you need a discount code that can't be abused.

cards.title: Use a starter template, then customize instead of building from scratch
cards.summary: Install a theme plus starter templates and Elementor so a full store layout exists before you customize.
cards.use_when: Building a new WordPress/WooCommerce storefront and you want a working layout fast.

cards.title: Elementor structure: sections, containers and widgets
cards.summary: Understand the three-level Elementor hierarchy and how to build a hero section from an empty canvas.
cards.use_when: Editing the homepage or a landing page in Elementor and you need to control layout and positioning.

cards.title: Style buttons for visibility: normal vs hover states, padding, radius
cards.summary: Configure button normal and hover states, padding and border radius so the CTA stands out on the page.
cards.use_when: Designing add-to-cart or buy-now buttons on a homepage, landing page or product page.

cards.title: Video and image hero sections on the homepage
cards.summary: Use an Elementor section with a video or gradient background, then fix contrast so overlaid text stays readable.
cards.use_when: Building or replacing the homepage hero that showcases a top product.

cards.title: Header and footer are theme settings, not Elementor
cards.summary: Edit the Astra header via Customize (logo, menu, transparent header) while page content stays in Elementor.
cards.use_when: Changing the store logo, navigation menu or header background color.

cards.title: Organize the catalog with product categories and parent/child structure
cards.summary: Create product categories (and parents) so shoppers can sort and categories surface on the homepage.
cards.use_when: Organizing a WooCommerce product catalog into navigable categories and subcategories before building collection menus and homepage sections.

cards.title: Upsells and cross-sells in WooCommerce linked products
cards.summary: Use WooCommerce Linked Products so shoppers see an upgrade on the product page and add-ons in the cart.
cards.use_when: Setting product recommendations on a PDP and in the cart to raise average order value.

cards.title: Clean up demo products before adding your own catalog
cards.summary: Delete template products and their trash, then replicate a configured product for the rest of the catalog instead of rebuilding each one.
cards.use_when: Starting a store from an imported template and needing to replace placeholder products.

cards.title: Responsive design: serve different sections per device in Elementor
cards.summary: Duplicate a desktop section and use Elementor's responsive controls to show a simplified version only on mobile.
cards.use_when: Fixing the homepage on mobile/tablet, e.g. a background video that doesn't play on phones.

cards.title: Single product page spacing and button styling via Customize
cards.summary: Fix PDP padding and recolor add-to-cart buttons in the Customizer rather than in Elementor.
cards.use_when: Adjusting layout and colors on the WooCommerce product page so content clears the header and CTAs match the brand.

cards.title: Edit Elementor sections with device-specific padding
cards.summary: Use Elementor's per-device padding controls and the mobile-only icon indicator to fix section spacing differently on mobile, tablet and desktop.
cards.use_when: Tuning store homepage, PDP or landing-page section spacing in Elementor so content isn't cut off or crammed on mobile while staying correct on desktop.

cards.title: Center misaligned Elementor widgets per breakpoint
cards.summary: Fix widgets that sit off to the left on mobile by setting their Style > Position to center within the mobile-only viewport.
cards.use_when: Correcting a call-to-action button, heading or image on a store landing page that looks left-aligned or off-center on phones after template import.

cards.title: Launch a WooCommerce store by switching from coming-soon to live
cards.summary: Take the WordPress/WooCommerce site out of store-coming-soon mode and save changes so shoppers can actually buy.
cards.use_when: Final go-live step after building and previewing a WooCommerce store, when checkout and product pages need to be publicly reachable.

cards.title: Customise an imported template by replacing images, colours and text
cards.summary: Build a store page faster by starting from a template and swapping images, text and colours rather than designing from scratch.
cards.use_when: Building a store homepage, category page or landing page quickly when a template already provides the section structure.

cards.title: Claim the $1/month trial link before the 3-day window closes
cards.summary: Sequence Shopify account creation so the extended promotional trial price is secured before the free trial expires.
cards.use_when: Opening a new Shopify account for a store build and choosing which plan to start on.

cards.title: Know which three Shopify admin areas actually run the store
cards.summary: Reduce admin overwhelm to Products, Online Store and Settings, the three sections that control selling, appearance and configuration.
cards.use_when: Orienting yourself in a new Shopify admin before adding products, designing the storefront or configuring checkout.

cards.title: Choose a clean, brandable domain instead of an over-thought one
cards.summary: Domain naming criteria that protect trust and ad click-through, plus an AI ideation method to avoid blank-page stalls.
cards.use_when: Selecting the store domain before running ads, email or packaging that will display the URL.

cards.title: Buy the domain inside Shopify vs. connecting an existing third-party domain
cards.summary: Two connection paths with different effort levels, plus the propagation window to plan your launch around.
cards.use_when: Setting up or migrating the store's domain before launch and before printing or advertising the URL.

cards.title: Pick and publish a lightweight free Shopify theme before customizing
cards.summary: Theme selection criteria and the preview-then-publish habit that prevents installing a look you have not seen.
cards.use_when: Choosing the storefront theme (fashion, beauty, large-catalog or general store) before any design work.

cards.title: Turn a default theme into a brand with global settings and a transparent logo
cards.summary: The fast foundational pass — hero H1, colors, typography, logo — that makes a template feel intentional before deeper section work.
cards.use_when: Customizing a freshly published theme so it stops looking generic and starts reading as a real brand.

cards.title: Structure header, menu style and announcement bar for product count
cards.summary: Match navigation pattern to catalog size and use a benefit-driven announcement bar to guide first actions.
cards.use_when: Configuring the storefront header, menus and announcement bar before driving traffic to the store.

cards.title: Build a hero banner that communicates one clear benefit
cards.summary: Hero image, headline, subtext and CTA decisions with a mobile contrast check.
cards.use_when: Designing or refining the homepage hero section — the first thing visitors see from ads or social traffic.

cards.title: Generate policies from Shopify templates and customize every detail
cards.summary: Use built-in policy templates, then edit shipping and refund specifics so disputes and chargebacks are reduced.
cards.use_when: Setting up privacy, terms, shipping and refund policies before the store accepts public orders.

cards.title: Write a product page by describing the product, then generating and rewriting the copy
cards.summary: Replace supplier text with benefit-led descriptions using Shopify's AI writing assistant plus short paragraphs and a brand-voice edit.
cards.use_when: Adding a product to the catalog and building the PDP copy that will carry conversion.

cards.title: Use compare-at pricing, variants and 1000px+ images on the product page
cards.summary: Pricing display, product options and image quality checks that shape perceived value and reduce refunds.
cards.use_when: Completing the pricing, options and imagery fields for each new product listing.

cards.title: Choose manual vs. automatic collections and surface them on the homepage
cards.summary: Collection type decision by catalog growth, plus the homepage section that gets products out of the backend.
cards.use_when: Organizing the catalog into browsable categories and featuring them on the homepage.

cards.title: Prune and rebuild the main menu around collections, then test it on mobile
cards.summary: Navigation hygiene as a conversion issue: remove defaults, add collections, verify on a phone.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up store navigation before launch so customers can actually find products.

cards.title: Order the homepage: hero, collections, featured products, then trust blocks
cards.summary: Sequence homepage sections so the page reads as guided rather than random, adding testimonials and an FAQ.
cards.use_when: Arranging or auditing homepage sections after products and collections exist.

cards.title: Activate Shopify Payments plus at least one alternative gateway
cards.summary: Payment setup that connects payouts and adds a familiar fallback option for hesitant and international buyers.
cards.use_when: Enabling payment methods before taking the store off password protection.

cards.title: Define shipping zones, rates and a free-shipping threshold
cards.summary: Zone, rate-model and threshold decisions that keep delivery expectations clear and lift average order value.
cards.use_when: Configuring shipping and delivery settings before launch, including whether to ship internationally.

cards.title: Configure taxes by verifying your own obligations first
cards.summary: Use Shopify's automatic tax tools, but establish nexus or VAT registration requirements before relying on them.
cards.use_when: Setting up tax collection for a store selling domestically or across borders.

cards.title: Install three apps, not ten — reviews, email, tracking
cards.summary: A lean app stack with a review tool chosen for free-plan strength versus photo-centric reviews.
cards.use_when: Adding apps to a new store without degrading page speed before launch.

cards.title: Run the pre-launch checklist: store details, domain, test order, mobile, policies, links
cards.summary: The final verification pass that catches small errors before the store goes public.
cards.use_when: The last step before removing password protection and making the store publicly accessible.

cards.title: Remove password protection and verify the live store as a customer
cards.summary: The publishing step plus a first-visitor walkthrough of the live domain.
cards.use_when: Taking the store public for the first time, immediately before sharing the link on social or with testers.

cards.title: Shopify backend launch order
cards.summary: Sequence the pre-launch Shopify backend tasks in the order that prevents rework: general settings, payments, shipping, policies, domain, then remove the storefront password.
cards.use_when: Preparing a newly built Shopify store to go live (final backend pass before publishing).

cards.title: Adding product variants for size and colour
cards.summary: Use Shopify's variant section to sell size/colour combinations, setting per-variant prices where larger sizes or colours should cost more.
cards.use_when: Product setup for an apparel store where one listing must cover multiple sizes or colours.

cards.title: Compare-at price strike-through
cards.summary: Enter a higher 'compare at' price so the product page shows the current price as a discount off a struck-through original.
cards.use_when: Pricing a product on its Shopify product page when you want visible discount framing.

cards.title: Inventory tracking and out-of-stock behaviour
cards.summary: Decide whether an item shows 'sold out' or keeps selling when inventory hits zero, based on whether you can actually restock on demand.
cards.use_when: Backend inventory setup for a store deciding how to handle a product running out.

cards.title: Manual collections: build category pages from a product list
cards.summary: Create manual collections so the storefront can show category pages (e.g. Shirts) and home-page grids built from hand-picked products.
cards.use_when: Organising products into shoppable categories for navigation and the home page.

cards.title: Delete default shipping zones before adding your own
cards.summary: Remove Shopify's default weight-based US zone and rates, then build your own zone and flat rates so pricing reflects your actual fulfilment.
cards.use_when: Shipping configuration on a new store where default rates do not match your shipping plan.

cards.title: Product shipping weight and box volume
cards.summary: Fill shipping weight and volume on products only if you intend to charge weight- or volume-based rates; flat-rate shippers can skip them.
cards.use_when: Product setup where you are deciding whether to populate shipping dimensions.

cards.title: Product description and imagery for the PDP
cards.summary: Write the title and description first, then add high-quality images and choose which one leads on the product page.
cards.use_when: Adding or improving a product listing on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Pre-launch asset preparation checklist
cards.summary: Prepare logo, favicon, colors, fonts and product/collection assets before touching the Shopify theme to avoid rework.
cards.use_when: You are about to build or rebuild a Shopify storefront and need to decide what to gather before starting theme customization.

cards.title: Choosing a Shopify plan by card rate and staff seats
cards.summary: Compare Basic, Grow and Advanced on card rates, staff seats and global/market features, and check legacy accounts separately.
cards.use_when: You are deciding which Shopify plan to subscribe to, or whether upgrading will pay for itself at your current sales volume.

cards.title: Store details, currency, and order numbering configuration
cards.summary: Set store name, contact email, billing region, currency and order ID settings so customer-facing notifications and localization are correct.
cards.use_when: You are in Shopify Settings > General during initial store setup and need to configure identity, currency and order numbering.

cards.title: Registering Shopify with your own owner email
cards.summary: Sign up with an email you control so you remain the store owner, then complete payment and business details in one pass.
cards.use_when: You are creating a new Shopify account, possibly with help from an agency or freelancer.

cards.title: Using role-based staff permissions instead of blanket access
cards.summary: Add staff users with custom roles scoped to exactly the admin areas they need, and use collaborator access as a cheaper workaround.
cards.use_when: You need to give an employee, contractor or agency access to your Shopify admin without exposing sales figures or settings.

cards.title: Connecting a custom domain and handling DNS records
cards.summary: Buy a .com domain early, connect it to Shopify, and learn to add DNS records yourself because future apps will require it.
cards.use_when: You are moving from the default myshopify.com URL to a branded customer-facing domain, or an app asks you to edit DNS records.

cards.title: Setting up store policies and return rules
cards.summary: Generate and customize privacy, terms, shipping, return/refund and contact policies, enable native return rules, and link them in the footer.
cards.use_when: You are preparing to launch or run ads and need legally presentable store policies plus a workable returns process.

cards.title: Choosing customer support tooling by catalog complexity
cards.summary: Start with the free Shopify Inbox and migrate to AI-assisted support once your catalog or product education demands scale.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how customers will ask pre-purchase questions and how you will answer them at launch versus at scale.

cards.title: Adding a product: title, description and image ratios
cards.summary: Fill product title/URL, keep the inline description short, and upload all images at one consistent ratio.
cards.use_when: You are creating a product record in Shopify before or alongside PDP design.

cards.title: Configuring product type, vendor, tags and category
cards.summary: Set type and tags with your future collection filters in mind, and pick a precise Shopify category to unlock extra metafields.
cards.use_when: You are adding products and want collections, filters and product attributes to work without rework.

cards.title: Pricing fields: compare-at and cost of goods
cards.summary: Use price, compare-at price and cost per item correctly so discount display works and margin calculations are possible later.
cards.use_when: You are setting product pricing or running a sale and want correct strikethrough display and usable cost data.

cards.title: Independent inventory, SKUs and warehouse coordination
cards.summary: Track inventory in Shopify with SKUs/barcodes so warehouses can match orders accurately, and understand available vs committed vs unavailable.
cards.use_when: You are setting stock levels and identifiers on a product, or preparing to hand fulfillment to a warehouse.

cards.title: Product weight, shipping profile and variants
cards.summary: Record a physical weight so Shopify does not treat the item as digital, and create variants for the option axes customers choose.
cards.use_when: You are completing the shipping section of a product and setting up size/color options for apparel or similar catalog.

cards.title: Defining brand assets in Shopify settings
cards.summary: Load logo, square logo, colors, cover image, slogan and social links into Store assets so the theme inherits them automatically.
cards.use_when: You are in Settings > General > Store assets and want theme customization to pull consistent branding without manual re-entry.
